title: ISO/IEC 30141:2024 — Internet of Things Reference Architecture — Scope
text:
ISO/IEC 30141:2024 — Internet of things (IoT) — Reference architecture (Edition 2.0, 2024-08)

Scope: Provides a standardized IoT Reference Architecture (IoT RA) using a common vocabulary, reusable designs, and industry best practices. The architecture covers IoT systems from multiple viewpoints: foundational, business, usage, functional, trustworthiness, and construction.

IoT Definition (from ISO/IEC 22989): infrastructure of interconnected entities, people, systems and information resources together with services that process and react to information from the physical world and virtual world.

Key IoT stakeholders: IoT service providers, IoT service developers, IoT service users, IoT device vendors, network operators, regulatory authorities.

The IoT RA applies to: smart cities, smart homes, smart industry (Industry 4.0/RAMI 4.0), healthcare IoT, connected vehicles, smart agriculture, energy management, and environmental monitoring.

title: IoT Reference Architecture — Foundational viewpoint and view
text:
ISO/IEC 30141:2024 — Clause 6.2: Foundational IoT viewpoint and view

The foundational IoT view defines the fundamental structural elements of any IoT system:

IoT component: basic building block of an IoT system with capabilities including:
- Interaction capability: communication with other components
- Processing capability: data computation and transformation
- Sensing and actuation capability: physical world interface
- Storage capability: data persistence
- Management capability: self-management and configuration

IoT system: collection of IoT components providing IoT functionalities.
IoT environment: broader context in which IoT systems operate.

Key relationships:
- IoT devices connect to IoT gateways
- IoT gateways connect to IoT platforms/cloud
- IoT applications consume data from IoT platforms

IoT component pattern (Clause 6.7.3): standardized pattern describing how IoT components interact, including: device capabilities, gateway functions, platform services, application interfaces.

title: IoT Reference Architecture — Business, usage, functional and trustworthiness viewpoints
text:
ISO/IEC 30141:2024 — Clauses 6.3-6.6: Multiple IoT viewpoints

6.3 Business viewpoint: IoT business concerns including service models, monetization, stakeholder relationships, regulatory compliance, and value chains. Addresses: IoT service provider roles, contractual relationships, business process integration.

6.4 Usage viewpoint: How IoT systems are used by stakeholders. Covers: use cases, usage scenarios, user interactions, accessibility, human factors. Examples: remote monitoring, automated control, predictive maintenance, asset tracking.

6.5 Functional viewpoint: IoT system functional decomposition.
External-facing functions: sensing, actuation, communication, data storage, data processing.
Internal abstract function classes: device management, network management, data management, service management, security management, operations support.

6.6 Trustworthiness viewpoint: IoT trustworthiness properties.
- Security: protection against unauthorized access, data integrity, confidentiality
- Safety: protection of physical environment and human health
- Privacy: protection of personally identifiable information (PII)
- Reliability: consistent correct behaviour
- Resilience: recovery from failures and attacks
- Common characteristics (Annex C): legacy support, network connectivity, unique identification, well-defined components, auto-configuration, content-awareness, context-awareness, discoverability, manageability, real-time capability, self-description, service subscription.

title: IoT Reference Architecture — Construction viewpoint and IoT patterns
text:
ISO/IEC 30141:2024 — Clause 6.7 and Annex A: Construction viewpoint and additional IoT patterns

6.7 Construction viewpoint: Physical and logical deployment architecture.
- IoT architecture construction view: layered architecture (device, network, platform, application)
- IoT component pattern: reusable architectural patterns for IoT components

Annex A — Additional IoT construction patterns:

A.2 RAMI 4.0 pattern (Reference Architecture Model Industrie 4.0):
- Three-dimensional architecture for Industry 4.0 / smart manufacturing
- Axes: layers (business, functional, information, communication, integration, asset), life cycle, hierarchy levels
- Supports digital twin concepts and manufacturing automation

A.3 Dynamic IoT system pattern: supports dynamic addition/removal of IoT devices at runtime.

A.4 IoT enterprise system pattern: integration of IoT with enterprise IT systems (ERP, CRM, MES).

A.5 IoT enterprise networking pattern: network architecture for enterprise IoT deployments.

A.6 IoT enterprise usage pattern: usage scenarios for enterprise IoT implementations including roles and activities.

Security considerations: IoT security must address device authentication, encrypted communication, secure boot, firmware integrity, access control, and audit logging — all aligning with ISO/IEC 27001 A.8 controls.
